# EC49FPD — Four complete native BRC 77-configuration domains; optimal adaptive depth four

Date: 2026-11-15. Status: AUTHOR_PROVED / EXACT_FINITE_CHECKED / NOT_REVIEWED. Frozen science pin: fc0f038e7bfd12c886b4d37f900bfb770c0f61ab. Original corpus SHA256: cd9a50799536d2b96230777b5392b1d742ceee896da05bb49aa097cf351e1d5e. Reuses the exact source Trie cost convention of EC49FOR and follows EC49FPC, PR #2460.

## Model and exact statements

The original corpus contains 94 signed/named key families, 178,850 byte-prefix words, 38,169 seven-key configurations and 24 labeled demands, whose complete legal-root signatures form 625 named domain classes. Named roots are 03, 05, 06 and 07. For configuration K and named root r, P_K(r,S) is the exact minimum signed/named-byte-prefix Trie coverage cost for root r's mandatory labels plus attainable optional subset S. For complete legal allocation a, T_K(a)=sum_r P_K(r,S_r(a)). The cost unit is the original native Trie integer unit, preserving each root and the actual source codewords.

**Theorem 1.** Within each entire named legal-root class whose least original configuration index is 16860, 16864, 16988 or 17022, for every pair A,B, equality of all complete assignment costs T_A(a)=T_B(a) holds if and only if all attainable named-root costs P_A(r,S)=P_B(r,S). The forward implication in this four-class theorem is certified by exhaustive finite classification of every configuration pair; the reverse implication is the defining sum.

| Class representative | Configurations | Complete actions/config | Root coordinates/config | Distinct P and T profiles | P-equal and T-equal pairs | Nonzero hidden gauge |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 16860 | 77 | 1296 | 340 | 31 | 1036 | 0 |
| 16864 | 77 | 1296 | 336 | 39 | 704 | 0 |
| 16988 | 77 | 1296 | 336 | 39 | 704 | 0 |
| 17022 | 77 | 1296 | 340 | 31 | 1036 | 0 |

Totals: **4 complete classes, 308 configurations, 104,104 root costs, 399,168 exact allocation costs, 11,704 within-class unordered pairs and 3,480 equal pairs** under either complete cost vector. Exact member lists are recomputed from all 38,169 source configurations, rather than selected by sampling.

**Theorem 2.** Suppose an unknown profile is promised to belong to the distinct P-profiles of one of the above full classes. Each terminal query chooses a complete legal allocation and reads the exact integer T(a); later queries may depend on previous results. The optimal worst-case adaptive query depths are **4,3,3,4**, in the class order above. There are exactly 1296 legal actions in each class. Constructive first query indices (zero-based) are respectively **1018,2,2,1020** in the product ordering of optional labels ascending, with roots 03,05,06,07 ascending.

## Proof of observation optimality

Let U be the finite unresolved subset of distinct P-profiles. A query q partitions U by its **exact integer** response T(q). Define feasible(U,0) iff |U|<=1; for d>=1, feasible(U,d) iff |U|<=1 or some complete query q has all of its response fibers feasible at depth d-1. Queries that do not split U can be discarded. Exhausting this recurrence is an exact decision-tree lower-bound proof; constructing and checking a successful tree is an upper-bound proof.

For 16864/16988, every depth-one and depth-two option is exhausted, and a depth-three decision tree resolves all 39 distinct profiles. For 16860/17022, every depth <=3 option is exhausted, and a depth-four tree resolves all 31 distinct profiles. Independent implementations use (a) exact pair-collision bitsets and second-query fibers and (b) a recursive partition search. For the two depth-four classes the 1296 queries induce **1251 different full-profile response partitions**. Retaining one action per identical partition is exact because all restrictions to subsequent candidate fibers remain identical. Each complete decision tree has been independently decoded against all underlying integer responses, with singleton final leaves.

This is the first verified depth-four example in this original EC49 finite line, extending depth-two and depth-three results of EC49FOZ and EC49FPC. The terminal observer is the finite all-allocations integer-cost interface; root-local information and future root-specific operations remain retained in P.

## Reproduction and provenance

The pinned raw source is the same as prior EC49FPC and EC49FOW evidence. Build the original EC49FOR C++17 byte-Trie extractor (in the EC49FPC evidence archive) with both -O2 and -O3. Provide the 308 IDs of the four classes and the exact frozen original corpus as stdin; both complete root-cost output tables have SHA256 **2e07ad0d935efd9824729feec6349c2af162e152cd9c8a2a93848fd4343eea93**, equal byte-for-byte. The locally run VERIFY_EC49FPD.py independently parses the original corpus, checks all 625 domain signatures and complete class membership, all P/T vectors, and recalculates all root-subset costs for two actual configurations per class using a second Python byte-prefix Trie implementation. ADAPTIVE_EC49FPD.py exhausts depth-two and constructs depth-three trees. ADAPTIVE4_EC49FPD.py exhausts depth-three and constructs depth-four trees. VERIFY_EC49FPD_CERTIFICATES.py independently walks every tree against all profiles.

The evidence archive EC49FPD_FOUR_77_DEPTH4_EVIDENCE_20261115.tar.xz contains the original input, all 104104 root records, both optimization-level outputs, code, full decision trees, logs and SHA256 manifest. This GitHub contribution records the manuscript, machine summary and reproducibility checker. Researcher identity, Activity checkpoint and formal task control are separate Source facts.

## Continuation

This advances the preceding **559 / 625** fully classified original legal-root classes to **563 / 625**, leaving 62 for complete classification. Next: size-87/101 classes, demand-subset-dependent higher-order cross-root gauge witnesses, and the minimal *fixed* (nonadaptive) number of terminal observations for the two depth-four classes. Earlier nonzero gauge witnesses in other legal-root classes remain valid with their own hypotheses.
